subject: Feature econ signal-to-cost mapping / next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: MedLytics discovery — unit‑econ signal-to-cost mapping

Folks — quick recap from this morning's 30m with Beth (MedLytics) and a short list of asks / next steps. Key points from the call: 

- High-level goal: embed three inference‑driven features in their provider workflow (Triage assist, Summary, Prior‑auth helper). They want predictable inference unit economics before committing to pilot.
- Rough token volume range (their estimate, attached): 50M — 120M tokens / month (depending on rollout breadth). They called out a near-term baseline of ~60–80M and a potential growth scenario to ~120M within 6–9 months. (See medlytics_token_estimates.xlsx)
- Budget signal: internal finance range they shared is $8k — $18k / month for inference.
- MedLytics target: $/1M tokens <= $150 to hit product margin goals (their stated margin target 55–65% net of inference).
- CAC / payback: they asked us to show a 6–9 month payback case for the first feature and a 9–12 month blended payback across the 3‑feature bundle.
- Per‑feature ask: they want an expected incremental inference cost per active user expressed as $/feature / month for pricing SKU mapping.

Actionable items (proposed):
1) Run 3 sensitivity scenarios in the unit econ workbook (low/mid/high token adoption) and surface: $/1M tokens, $/feature (monthly), gross margin at target price points, and CAC payback months.
2) Align on a target $/1M that lets them keep margin >=55% while meeting their $8k–$18k budget window.
3) Set a 30‑minute pricing workshop with Beth + procurement to walk the workbook and proposed pricing bands.

Attachments: medlytics_token_estimates.xlsx (their raw volumes). I attached the redwood_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx to populate scenarios — Marissa, can you take point on the scenarios and prepare 3 slides + the workbook?

Next meeting ask: 30 min pricing workshop — tentative week of 6/15. Beth said procurement will want a simple per‑feature $/month SKU and a 12‑month committed tier option.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(h) 415‑555‑0123
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: MedLytics discovery — unit‑econ signal-to-cost mapping

Thanks for the crisp recap — good signal from Beth. A few quick notes: 

- We should show both per‑1M token list price and an example per‑feature SKU that maps to expected active users (MAU) so procurement can run their own $/user math.
- Propose three pricing bands to test in the workshop: 
  * Standard (no commit) — conservative: $/1M = $195
  * Committed 12mo (mid) — $/1M = $140
  * Aggressive commit (annual + usage) — $/1M = $115
  These are rough; we'll tune after Marissa runs the workbook scenarios.
- For the CAC payback modeling: I'll draft a simple revenue mapping that ties feature price -> ARPU uplift -> payback months. If they insist on 6–9 months for the first feature we may need a combination of a small per‑feature setup fee + mid‑tier committed $/1M.

Marissa — can you: (1) fill the redwood_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx with the low/mid/high adoption scenarios; (2) output a one‑page slide per scenario (ppt/pdf); (3) add a sensitivity table for $/1M from $100–$220 so we can show margin and payback shifts.

I'll draft a 30 minute agenda for the pricing workshop and propose calendar slots.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Beth Nolan <beth.nolan@medlytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: MedLytics discovery — unit‑econ signal-to-cost mapping

Thanks Hannah — this matches our internal thinking. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: attached is the quick token estimate we used on the call (medlytics_token_estimates.xlsx). The baseline (pilot, 1 clinic chain) maps to ~58M tokens/mo. If we roll out across our mid‑market accounts within 6–9 months we get to ~110–125M tokens/mo.
- Budget: finance gave the $8k–$18k range as a direction; procurement would prefer committing to a 12mo band if it buys us a lower $/1M.
- $/1M target: we don't need the absolute lowest price, but we need to be <= $150/1M to maintain our margin targets (we're targeting 55–65% gross margin net of inference).
- CAC payback: our PM and finance are aligned around ~9 months as the realistic target for the first feature; 6 months is aggressive unless we offset with an onboarding fee or performance milestones.

Procurement contact: procurement@medlytics.com (please include them on the workshop invite).

Can you also include a brief canary/rollout suggestion for how we would measure inference cost per 1k users and a fallback plan if latency / cost spikes during rollout? That helps our ops and security folks.

Happy to do the workshop on 6/16 (afternoon PT) or 6/17 (morning PT).

Thanks,
Beth Nolan
Head of Product Operations, MedLytics
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Beth Nolan <beth.nolan@medlytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@medlytics.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap: MedLytics discovery — workshop prep and next steps

Forwarding Beth's confirmation and pulling this thread together for clarity. Short plan & owners: 

1) Marissa — fill the unit‑econ workbook with three scenarios (pilot = 58M, mid = 85M, ramp = 115M). Include columns: tokens/mo, expected requests per MAU, $/1M tokens, incremental $/feature / month, gross margin @ proposed retail price, payback months. Deliverable: workbook + 3 one‑page slides by 6/16 AM PT.
2) Ben — prepare a 30m workshop agenda and two pricing band proposals (committed 12mo vs month‑to‑month) and include example per‑feature SKUs and an onboarding fee option.
3) Hannah — I'll run the workshop and cover canary rollout + fallback policies (cache/KV thresholds, model fallback to lower‑cost variant) and bring the SLA summary (see redwood_pricing_tiers.pdf for standard terms).

Proposed workshop times (Beth suggested): 6/16 3:00–3:30pm PT or 6/17 9:00–9:30am PT. I'll send the calendar once Ben confirms agenda.

Marissa, attaching the redwood_unit_econ_workbook.xlsx and our pricing tiers PDF.

Thanks — aim here is to give procurement a tight set of scenarios that prove a committed tier at ~$140/1M meets their margin and payback targets; if not, we'll iterate on a small onboarding fee or blended price to bring payback down.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | san francisco, ca
